exercises.instruction: Choose the correctly punctuated non-defining relative clause.
options: My father who is an engineer built this house.
My father, who is an engineer, built this house.
My father, who is an engineer built this house.
My father who is an engineer, built this house.
exercises.answer: My father, who is an engineer, built this house.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining clauses need commas both before and after. The speaker has one father, so this is extra info.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun for a non-defining clause.
exercises.prompt: The Eiffel Tower, ___ was built in 1889, attracts millions of visitors each year.
options: that
which
who
whose
exercises.explanation: 'That' is not used in non-defining clauses. 'Which' is correct for a thing (the Eiffel Tower).

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence where 'which' correctly refers to the whole previous clause.
options: She missed the deadline which was surprising.
She missed the deadline, which was surprising.
She missed the deadline that was surprising.
She missed the deadline, that was surprising.
exercises.answer: She missed the deadline, which was surprising.
exercises.explanation: When 'which' refers to the entire preceding clause, a comma is required and 'that' cannot be used.

exercises.instruction: Identify the sentence with an error.
options: Dr Sari, who leads the department, will retire next year.
Jakarta, which is the capital city, has a population of over 10 million.
The CEO, that resigned last week, issued a statement.
My sister, whose husband is a pilot, lives in Singapore.
exercises.answer: The CEO, that resigned last week, issued a statement.
exercises.explanation: 'That' cannot be used in non-defining relative clauses. Use 'who' for a person.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence changes meaning when you add commas?
exercises.prompt: Compare: A) 'The employees who completed training received bonuses.' B) 'The employees, who completed training, received bonuses.'
options: They mean the same thing.
A means only trained employees got bonuses; B means all employees got bonuses.
A is grammatically correct; B is wrong.
B means only trained employees got bonuses; A means all employees got bonuses.
exercises.answer: A means only trained employees got bonuses; B means all employees got bonuses.
exercises.explanation: Defining (no commas) = only employees who completed training. Non-defining (commas) = all employees completed training and all got bonuses.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence correctly uses 'whose' in a non-defining clause?
options: The professor whose research was cited will give a keynote.
The professor, whose research was cited, will give a keynote.
The professor, who's research was cited, will give a keynote.
The professor, which research was cited, will give a keynote.
exercises.answer: The professor, whose research was cited, will give a keynote.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' = possessive. The professor is already identified (likely by context), so commas are used. 'Who's' = who is — wrong.

exercises.instruction: Choose the non-defining clause that adds location information.
exercises.prompt: Yogyakarta, ___ the famous Borobudur temple is located, is a major tourist destination.
options: that
which
who
where
exercises.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places. Yogyakarta is already identified — this is extra information.

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence that correctly uses a non-defining clause with 'when'.
options: 2020, when the pandemic started, changed the world.
2020, that the pandemic started, changed the world.
In 2020, which the pandemic started, changed the world.
In 2020, when the pandemic started, many businesses closed.
exercises.answer: In 2020, when the pandemic started, many businesses closed.
exercises.explanation: 'When' refers to the time (2020). 'In 2020, when...' is the natural structure for a time-based non-defining clause.

exercises.instruction: Choose the defining clause (no commas needed).
options: My brother, who is a doctor, works at a hospital.
The doctor who treated me yesterday was very professional.
Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin, was Scottish.
The sun, which is a star, provides energy to Earth.
exercises.answer: The doctor who treated me yesterday was very professional.
exercises.explanation: No commas — 'who treated me yesterday' identifies WHICH doctor. This is a defining clause.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'which' or 'that'. The clause is non-defining.
exercises.prompt: The Great Wall of China, ___ stretches over 21,000 kilometres, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
options: did which
which
whichs
whiching
exercises.explanation: Non-defining clause → 'that' is not allowed. Use 'which' for a thing.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the missing punctuation. Write the two missing commas as: ', ,'
exercises.prompt: My colleague ___ who joined last month ___ has already impressed the team.
options: commas
, who joined last month,
exercises.hint: Non-defining clauses are set off by commas on both sides.
exercises.explanation: Commas required before and after the non-defining clause: 'My colleague, who joined last month, has already impressed the team.'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct relative pronoun. The clause refers to the entire previous statement.
exercises.prompt: She was promoted to manager, ___ came as a surprise to everyone.
options: whiching
whichs
which
did which
exercises.explanation: 'Which' refers to the entire previous clause (her promotion). A comma is required before it.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'who' or 'which'.
exercises.prompt: Professor Tan, ___ has published over 50 papers, will retire next semester.
options: did who
whoing
whos
who
exercises.explanation: Professor Tan is a person → 'who'. This is a non-defining clause (proper noun = already identified).

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'whose' or 'who's'.
exercises.prompt: The artist, ___ latest exhibition opened last week, has received international acclaim.
options: whoseing
whoses
whose
did whose
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' = possessive (the exhibition belongs to the artist). 'Who's' = who is — incorrect here.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Ibu saya, yang adalah seorang guru, sudah pensiun."
exercises.prompt: Ibu saya, yang adalah seorang guru, sudah pensiun.
options: My mother, who is a teacher, has retired.
My mother, who is a teacher, have retired.
My mother, who is an teacher, has retired.
My mother, who was a teacher, has retired.
exercises.answer: My mother, who is a teacher, has retired.
exercises.explanation: 'Yang' after 'Ibu saya' (my mother) is non-defining — she is unique. Use commas and 'who'.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Dia lulus ujian dengan nilai sempurna, yang mengejutkan semua orang."
exercises.prompt: Dia lulus ujian dengan nilai sempurna, yang mengejutkan semua orang.
options: She passed an exam with a perfect score, which surprised everyone.
She passed the exam with a perfect score, which surprised everyone.
She passed the exam with an perfect score, which surprised everyone.
She passed exam with perfect score, which surprised everyone.
exercises.answer: She passed the exam with a perfect score, which surprised everyone.
exercises.explanation: 'Yang' here refers to the whole previous clause (the act of passing) — use ', which'.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Gojek, yang didirikan pada 2010, kini menjadi salah satu unicorn terbesar di Asia Tenggara."
exercises.prompt: Gojek, yang didirikan pada 2010, kini menjadi salah satu unicorn terbesar di Asia Tenggara.
options: Gojek, which was founded in 2010, was now one of the largest unicorns in Southeast Asia.
Gojek, which was founded in 2010, is now one of the largest unicorns in Southeast Asia.
Gojek, which was founded in 2010, is now one of a largest unicorns in Southeast Asia.
Gojek, which is founded in 2010, is now one of the largest unicorns in Southeast Asia.
exercises.answer: Gojek, which was founded in 2010, is now one of the largest unicorns in Southeast Asia.
exercises.explanation: Proper noun (Gojek) → non-defining clause. Use 'which' for a company. Add commas.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Bandung, di mana saya dibesarkan, adalah kota yang indah."
exercises.prompt: Bandung, di mana saya dibesarkan, adalah kota yang indah.
options: Bandung, where I grew up, is beautiful city.
Bandung, where I grew up, is a beautiful city.
Bandung, where I grew up, was a beautiful city.
Bandung, where I grew up, is an beautiful city.
exercises.answer: Bandung, where I grew up, is a beautiful city.
exercises.explanation: 'Di mana' → 'where'. Bandung is a proper noun → non-defining → commas.

exercises.instruction: What does the non-defining clause version mean?
exercises.prompt: 'The researchers, who had tested three hypotheses, published their findings.' vs. 'The researchers who had tested three hypotheses published their findings.'
options: Both sentences mean the same thing.
The comma version = all researchers tested three hypotheses; no comma = only those who tested three published.
The no-comma version = all researchers; comma version = only some researchers.
Both are grammatically incorrect.
exercises.answer: The comma version = all researchers tested three hypotheses; no comma = only those who tested three published.
exercises.explanation: Commas (non-defining) = extra info about all researchers. No commas (defining) = identifies which subset of researchers published.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correctly written sentence with a non-defining clause at the end.
exercises.prompt: Normal: 'She works at Google. Google offers excellent benefits.'
options: She works at Google that offers excellent benefits.
She works at Google, that offers excellent benefits.
She works at Google, which offers excellent benefits.
She works at Google which offers excellent benefits.
exercises.answer: She works at Google, which offers excellent benefits.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining clause at the end: comma before 'which'. 'That' is not used in non-defining clauses.
